doc.title: Arthur Davis and Andy Mosley Interview, 1960-01-12

title: Learning guitar at Angola; music near Tuskegee
summary: Asked about instruments, he says he learned guitar since coming to Angola, and recalls hearing work songs and Tuskegee Institute music in Alabama.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Do you play any musical instruments in addition to singing?

Yes. Well, I've learned music since I've been here. But I've only finished a field and I just pick up a few chords and sing with the chords that I play behind. What instrument is that now? It's guitar. Guitar. Now, what kind of music do you remember hearing when you were a kid over there in Alabama? Well, they have all instruments. I live in the neighborhood of Tuskegee Institute and they have all the sax perform, guitar, trumpet, piano. You didn't hear anything like this over there? No, no more than after I've grown up, I worked at plays that most men sang those type of songs seeming to me to make the day go short or something. It's just an old routine and I picked up the air from hearing those fellas sing. Here comes a good one, early in the morning.
